# A change can be permanently blocked by a stale LLM-Review -1

When `LLM-Review` votes -1 for a reason that is later RESOLVED OUTSIDE the diff — the
`bugfix-size-attestation` finding is the concrete case: it blocks on the ticket lacking a
plan-review attestation, which is earned by running `rebar review-plan`, not by editing code —
there is no reliable way to get the vote recomputed. The change cannot land even though the
finding no longer holds.

## The copy condition swallows every re-trigger
    copy condition: "changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE OR changekind:MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE
                     OR changekind:TRIVIAL_REBASE"

Observed on change 1577 (bug 85fa), four attempts, all copied the stale -1 rather than
re-reviewing:
  1. `git commit --amend --no-edit` + push  -> same tree AND message -> NO_CODE_CHANGE -> copied
  2. commit-MESSAGE-only amend + push      -> still NO_CODE_CHANGE (tree unchanged) -> copied
  3. `recheck-review` comment (documented in docs/review-policy.md:47) -> the review bot did
     not respond; it also CANCELLED the in-flight CI run, leaving a spurious Verified -1
  4. rebase onto current main + push       -> TRIVIAL_REBASE -> copied

CI behaves differently and correctly: `Verified` re-ran on patch sets 3 and 4. Only the LLM
review is stuck, which makes the asymmetry easy to miss.

The remaining levers per docs/review-policy.md are a maintainer re-trigger or a genuine
content change. Manufacturing a code edit purely to defeat vote-copying is a bad incentive: it
adds unreviewed churn to satisfy a mechanism, not a reviewer.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than working around
The gate stack already taxes small fixes. On 85fa: a ~70-line correctness fix hit the 800-line
module cap, which forced a module extraction, which pushed it to 321 non-test lines, which
tripped the 150-line bugfix floor, which required an LLM plan review to clear — and then the
resulting -1 could not be recomputed once the attestation existed. Three gates compounding,
with no exit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] ~~ A blocked author can cause LLM-Review to re-evaluate the CURRENT patch set without~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      changing code — e.g. `recheck-review` actually re-runs the reviewer, mirroring what
      `recheck` does for CI.
- [x] ~~ If `recheck-review` is the intended mechanism, it works and is tested; if it is not,~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      docs/review-policy.md stops naming it.
- [x] ~~ A re-trigger comment does not CANCEL a running CI job (observed: posting~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      `recheck-review` cancelled run 31349189893 and produced a Verified -1 that reflected
      cancellation, not a real failure).
- [x] ~~ Consider narrowing the copy condition: a finding whose evidence lives OUTSIDE the diff~~ — SUPERSEDED, not delivered here
      (attestation state on the ticket) should not be copied forward across patch sets, since
      the world it described can change without the tree changing.

## DUPLICATE — superseded by bug 6a81
Filed before finding the existing tickets. The acceptance criteria above are NOT
delivered by this ticket; they are struck through and carried by:
  6a81  recheck-review should accept a bugfix-size-attestation block once the ticket
        has the attestation  (the primary issue; my findings are recorded there)
  0d78  Prevent recheck-review from retriggering CI  (the cancellation side effect)
  b0f5  /rerun and recheck-review are fire-and-forget into a volatile queue  (why the
        re-trigger produced no reviewer response at all)
